state.title: mvn -q -P jvm-only test

parts.text:
Maven jvm-only test succeeded (no error; output logs). Good.

Now, we should run `cargo test` for affected crates only (we did) and maybe skip Qt. The full workspace hung at Qt tests; we can note. We need maybe run `cargo test -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-html ...` already passed. Good.

Now, check `git diff` for `pathland-ts-codegen` and ensure codegen test maybe. Run `cargo test -p pathland-ts-codegen`? Probably no tests. Maybe `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` already.

Now, manual review of Kotlin `ListStyle` and `List` for API quality:
- `ListStyle.Configuration` has `content` and `itemCount`; `makeBody` default returns content. Good.
- `ListStyle.RowConfiguration.selected` is a `Signal<Boolean>`, and `isSelected()` reads it. Good.
- The Kotlin style is a `Style` which extends `ViewModifier`; `.listStyle` wraps. Good.
- `selected` modifier added; this is a new public modifier not in spec. We added spec? We added `listStyle` modifier row, but not `selected`. Should we document `selected`? It's a general semantic modifier useful. The spec's modifier list doesn't include it. We should add a row for `selected`? Maybe not necessary, but it's public API. We added it primarily for internal List. Could make it internal instead of public to avoid undocumented surface. But it's useful. Let's add to spec modifier table:
`| selected | .selected(_:) | .selected(boolean) / .selected(signal) | SELECTED 0x2004 |` in interaction state section. This is a legitimate modifier. Also add to Rust? Rust has `bind_value_bool` for `SELECTED` used by Toggle; no generic `selected` modifier. For parity maybe add Rust `Selected` modifier? Not required. But public Kotlin `selected` should be documented. Add row.

- `ListRowView` calls `.selected(selected)` which uses `Modified.prop(Properties.SELECTED, signal)`. `ReactiveValues.initial` for bool signal likely works. The test checked `SELECTED` property count? In static list test, we asserted ROLE count but not SELECTED. Could add assertion that SELECTED property emitted. Let's add to ListTest static test `propertyIds(frame).count { it == Properties.SELECTED } == 2`? Emitter might emit SELECTED once per row. Good. Add? Not necessary but validates.

- `ListStyle` in Rust doesn't implement `ViewModifier`; no `.selected`. Fine.

- Did we add List to `AGENTS.md`? Not necessary.

- Did we update `spec/DSL.md` §4.2 `List` table with `ListStyle` and `List` row? yes.

- Did we update `spec/TOKENS.md` `color.selection` to Tier 2, while `color.selection` is used by Tier1 list tokens. Fine.

- Did we update `design/scripts/check.mjs`? No, generic.

- Did we update `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` to mention native list widgets? yes.

state.output: # @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 25, 2026 The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client, replacing the duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract: `spec/`. ## Implemented - **Decoder hardening (issue #63)**: `parseBatch`/`readString`/`readList`/ `readEntryBytes`/`readAttributed` enforce opcode, string-section, list, run/link/attribute, and text-range caps; `applyBatch` validates the whole batch structurally before mutating the DOM (no half-applied batch, unknown value types rejected). Attributed-text links and image/media sources are URL-scheme allowlisted (`javascript:` and non-media `data:` rejected). The transport rejects inbound messages over 2 MiB and closes after five consecutive malformed batches so the reconnect path requests a clean `META::RESYNC`. **SRI**: `copy-to-libs` writes a `sha384-…` second manifest line; the server emits `integrity` on the script tag. - **Attributed text**: decodes `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` payloads and applies them to the hydrated text element as styled ``/`` runs (v1 attributes: font size/weight/color/style/design/underline/strikethrough). An explicit `SET_TEXT` clears the rich-text marker; plain `TEXT`/`LABEL` updates never wipe rich spans. Full rebuild on payload change; the optional surgical `Range` fast path is deferred. - **Window metadata**: the DOM client applies `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` at runtime — `TITLE` → `document.title`, `DESCRIPTION` → meta description, `LOCALE` → ``; empty clears to the renderer default. `LABEL` also names buttons and slider inputs; the media shell is `aria-hidden`. - **Keyboard focus (ADR-0018)**: `META::SET_FOCUS` focuses/blurs a node by id; `A=0, B=0` clears the currently focused element. A node whose `EVENT_LISTENERS` carries the `FOCUS` bit gets `tabindex="0"` (and a `data-pathland-focusable` marker); removing it clears the tab stop. `FOCUS_CHANGED` is reported for any focused node (editing remains text-input only). `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` map native keys to the canonical table and suppress the platform default for arrows/Home/End/Paging/Enter/Space while leaving Tab native. Scroll containers are `tabindex="-1"` so the focused row owns the tab stop. - **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and `npm run copy-to-libs` copies it into the Quarkus extension and Spring Boot starter jars' static resource dirs under a **content-hashed name** (`dom-renderer-.js`), pruning stale `dom-renderer-*.js` and the pre-hash literal `dom-renderer.js` (the old duplicated `app.js` is long since removed). A pointer manifest `dom-renderer.current` sits next to the copies (content-hashed name + a `sha384-…` SRI digest); the SSR layer reads it (`PathlandAssets`) to emit the right `

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.scaledToFill

/**
 * The now-playing sidebar (right): the current track's large album art, its
 * title/artist, and the next two tracks. An optional [adUrl] appends a
 * sponsored slot embedding a second Pathland app via a ProxyView.
 */
internal class NowPlayingSidebar(
    private val adUrl: String?,
) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 14f) {
            Text("Now Playing")
                .fontSize(18f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
                .accessibilityRole(Roles.HEADER)

            Image(computed { service.currentTrack.get().cover })
                .frame(width = 220f, height = 220f)
                .scaledToFill()
                .border {
                    color(Color.BLACK)
                    width(1f)
                    radius(8f)
                }

            Text(computed { service.currentTrack.get().title })
                .fontSize(20f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)

            Text(computed {
                val track = service.currentTrack.get()
                "${track.artist} · ${track.album}"
            }).foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)

            Divider().padding(top = 0f, right = 0f, bottom = 10f, left = 0f)

            Text("Up Next").fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
            UpNextRowView(1)
            UpNextRowView(2)

            if (adUrl != null) {
                ProxyView(endpoint = adUrl, route = "/")
                    .frame(width = 220f, height = 140f)
            }
        }.padding(24f)
            .background(MusicPlayerView.SIDEBAR_BG)
            .frame(width = MusicPlayerView.SIDEBAR_WIDTH, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
    }
}

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 22, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-core`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
It owns the app-driven music player and the small sponsored-proxy ad app.

## Structure

- `music/` — the root `MusicPlayerView` (public, Java-mountable).
- `music/model/` — `Track`, `Lyrics`.
- `music/library/` — `LibraryView`, `TrackRowView`.
- `music/player/` — `PlayerMainArea`, `PlayerBar`, `PlayerControls`,
  `TransportControls`, `TrackInfoView`, `VolumeControls`.
- `music/player/controls/` — `SeekControl`, `PercentSeek`, `VolumeControl`.
- `music/service/` — `MediaPlayerService`: per-session player state, playlist,
  `MediaController`, and the environment key shared by the views.
- `music/lyrics/` — `SubtitlePill`.
- `music/sidebar/` — `NowPlayingSidebar`, `UpNextRowView`.
- `ad/` — `AdView`.

## Shared demo support

- **`DemoTheme`** — the demo's global `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` theme (base + `dark.*`).
- **`DemoAssets`** — the single embedded copy of the 8 audio tracks, 8 album
  covers, and 8 lyric SRT files under
  `META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/`, plus temp-dir extraction for hosts.
- **`DemoAssetsTest`** — guards all 32 embedded assets and extraction.
- **Responsive-size cover assets** — full 440×440 JPEGs remain for the 220×220
  sidebar; separate 176×176 JPEG thumbnails are used by the smaller track-row
  and player-bar images. Both sets are embedded and extracted for web and GTK.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `ViewThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume, compact play-only transport), medium (volume), or
  wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`), with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
  and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
- **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
  `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
  candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command (each in its own file under `player/controls/`).
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app: a title, a button, and a
  persisted click counter (`ad.clicks`), fully Kotlin-owned and Java-mountable.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.
- **Windowed library** — `LibraryView` is a `ScrollView` over a `LazyVStack` +
  paged `ForEach` with a fixed 64 pt row extent; `MediaPlayerService` repeats the
  eight base tracks into a 1000-entry playlist and serves 50-row pages with a
  small simulated latency. Loaded rows render `TrackRowView` (a tappable `HStack`
  highlighted by absolute index); unloaded rows render a skeleton placeholder.
  The live/SSR session uses the `PagedDataSource`; emitter-only unit-test mounts
  keep the in-memory list for determinism. The engine's reactive prefetch keeps
  rows rendered ahead of fast scrolling; the demo has no overscan setting.
  Visible-range reports are coalesced latest-wins and stale pages are cached
  without rendering, so a fast scrollbar drag back and forth reuses the visited
  windows instead of showing blank rows and refetching (ADR-0017).
  **Keyboard library navigation (ADR-0018)** — the library uses the shared
  `LazySelection` component: one roving `FOCUS` tab stop on the service's
  ephemeral `focusedIndex`; ↑/↓/Home/End move it, Enter/tap play, Space toggles
  playback. Selection never requests native focus while the list is unfocused,
  so scrolling/clamping cannot steal focus; tapping a row selects and focuses it
  synchronously before playback. Loaded and skeleton rows share the component's
  wrapper; placeholder rows are keyboard-focusable too. The selected row uses a
  blue background while the list is focused and a neutral gray background while
  it is not; text stays black when unfocused. Every row keeps a stable leading
  speaker icon child and the current track reveals it by opacity, so switching
  tracks cannot accumulate stale icons. List rows use the selected background
  as their keyboard indicator and suppress the generic focus outline. Native player-bar controls
  are explicitly tabbable, so Tab leaves the list and reaches the transport
  controls/seek slider under Safari's default keyboard-nav setting as well as
  Chrome. The volume slider carries an explicit 5% `STEP_VALUE`, so each arrow
  press moves it audibly; the seek slider stays continuous (1% per arrow).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MediaPlayerServiceTest` (persisted keys, select/next/previous, the 1000-entry
repeated library), `MusicPlayerViewTest` (tree/render, fit swaps, media state,
seek echo guard, snapshot emission, sponsored proxy, and the bounded lazy
library window), `MusicPlayerFitMediaTest` (the pinned media controller survives SSR
snapshot→live and repeated fit crossings; media routing and play stay bound),
and `AdViewTest` (button click / persisted counter delta).

## Phase 6 — Demos + status ✅ (runnable in the browser)

20. ✅ The initial route is part of the **platform environment** (user-driven
    design revision): `META::ENVIRONMENT` became the extensible field family
    (`VIEWPORT_WIDTH`/`VIEWPORT_HEIGHT`/`ROUTE`, spec/OPCODE.md §Environment
    fields). **SSR** synthesizes it from the HTTP request (catch-alls in both
    demos); the **DOM client** sends it (viewport + route) as its first WS
    message and **enriches** it after connect (window-resize re-emits viewport).
    Sessions are created **lazily on the first message** so the router seeds
    from the `ROUTE` field before mount — deep links render correctly on the
    first frame and the WS tree stays consistent with the SSR HTML.
21. ✅ The Kotlin demo views: `MusicPlayerView` is the demo root (sidebar + content;
    `/kitchen` keeps the showcase); both `SessionApp` apply the environment
    (seed + `applyEnvironment` enrichment) and forward `NAVIGATE` events.
22. ✅ **Verified in the browser**: both demos run; `curl /kitchen` → the
    kitchen-sink content + `data-pathland-route="/kitchen"`; `/home`/`/settings`
    content; unknown paths → sidebar + "Not Found"; JS bundle served. 76 Java
    tests + 61 TS tests + core vectors 26–27 green.
23. ✅ **status.md updates** (per AGENTS.md): `pathland-core`,
    `pathland-core-transport`, `lib/java/pathland-view-core`, `pathland-render-html`,
    `lib/typescript` — in their landing changes.

### Fix (post-Phase-6): SPA catch-all no longer shadows `/ws`

The deep-link catch-all initially matched `/ws`, so the WebSocket handshake was
package dev.pathland.demo.music.library

import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
import dev.pathland.demo.music.model.Track
import dev.pathland.demo.music.service.MediaPlayerService
import dev.pathland.demo.music.service.mediaPlayerService
import dev.pathland.view.core.Color
import dev.pathland.view.core.FontWeight
import dev.pathland.view.core.HorizontalAlignment
import dev.pathland.view.core.IconName
import dev.pathland.view.core.VerticalAlignment
import dev.pathland.view.core.View
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Commands
import dev.pathland.view.core.TextAlignment
import dev.pathland.view.core.Roles
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.HStack
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Icon
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Image
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Component
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Spacer
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.VStack
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.accessibilityRole
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.background
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.computed
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontSize
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontWeight
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.foregroundStyle
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.frame
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.lineLimit
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.multilineTextAlignment
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.opacity
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.scaledToFit

/**
 * A single track row: a playing indicator gutter, cover thumbnail, title/artist,
 * and duration. The selected row is highlighted; the current track's fixed
 * speaker icon is revealed by opacity. Both states are independent and
 * reactive.
 */
internal class TrackRowView(
    private val track: Track,
    private val index: Int,
) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val isCurrent = computed { service.trackIndex.get() == index }
        val isSelected = computed { service.focusedIndex.get() == index }
        val isListFocused = computed { service.listFocused.get() }
        val bg = computed {
            when {
                !isSelected.get() -> Color.CLEAR
                isListFocused.get() -> MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_BG
                else -> MusicPlayerView.INACTIVE_ROW_BG
            }
        }
        val fg = computed {
            if (isSelected.get() && isListFocused.get()) MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG else Color.BLACK
        }
        val playingIconOpacity = computed { if (isCurrent.get()) 1f else 0f }

        return HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 12f) {
            // Keep this child stable: only its opacity changes, so a previous
            // playing track can never leave a stray icon behind.
            Icon(IconName.VOLUME)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
                .opacity(playingIconOpacity)

            Image(track.thumbnail)
                .frame(width = 44f, height = 44f)
                .scaledToFit()

            VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 2f) {
                Text(track.title)
                    .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)

                Text("${track.artist} · ${track.album}")
                    .fontSize(13f)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
            }

            Spacer()

            Text(MediaPlayerService.fmt(track.duration))
                .fontSize(13f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
        }
            .accessibilityRole(Roles.LIST_ITEM)
            .background(bg)
            .foregroundStyle(fg)
            .padding(6f)
            .frame { width(Commands.Size.FILL) }
    }
}

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.opacity
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.scaledToFit

/**
 * A single track row: a playing indicator gutter, cover thumbnail, title/artist,
 * and duration. The selected row is highlighted; the current track's fixed
 * speaker icon is revealed by opacity. Both states are independent and
 * reactive.
 */
internal class TrackRowView(
    private val track: Track,
    private val index: Int,
) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val isCurrent = computed { service.trackIndex.get() == index }
        val isSelected = computed { service.focusedIndex.get() == index }
        val isListFocused = computed { service.listFocused.get() }
        val bg = computed {
            when {
                !isSelected.get() -> Color.CLEAR
                isListFocused.get() -> MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_BG
                else -> MusicPlayerView.INACTIVE_ROW_BG
            }
        }
        val fg = computed {
            if (isSelected.get() && isListFocused.get()) MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG else Color.BLACK
        }
        val playingIconOpacity = computed { if (isCurrent.get()) 1f else 0f }

        return HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 12f) {
            // Keep this child stable: only its opacity changes, so a previous
            // playing track can never leave a stray icon behind.
            Icon(IconName.VOLUME)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
                .opacity(playingIconOpacity)

            Image(track.thumbnail)
                .frame(width = 44f, height = 44f)
                .scaledToFit()

            VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 2f) {
                Text(track.title)
                    .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)

                Text("${track.artist} · ${track.album}")
                    .fontSize(13f)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
            }

            Spacer()

            Text(MediaPlayerService.fmt(track.duration))
                .fontSize(13f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
        }
            .accessibilityRole(Roles.LIST_ITEM)
            .background(bg)
            .foregroundStyle(fg)
            .padding(6f)
            .frame { width(Commands.Size.FILL) }
    }
}

package dev.pathland.demo.music

import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Categories
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Commands
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Components
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Opcode
import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Properties
import dev.pathland.view.core.Keys
import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.StateStore
import dev.pathland.core.transport.Event
import dev.pathland.core.transport.FrameOpcodeSink
import dev.pathland.core.transport.ProtocolFrame
import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
import dev.pathland.demo.music.library.LIBRARY_ROW_HEIGHT
import dev.pathland.demo.music.service.MediaPlayerService
import dev.pathland.view.engine.InputDispatcher
import dev.pathland.view.engine.RenderResult
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

/**
 * The music player demo: a track library, now-playing sidebar with album art,
 * and a bottom player bar. Asserts the rendered tree and that interactions drive
 * the persisted player state.
 */
class MusicPlayerViewTest {

    private data class Mounted(
        val result: RenderResult,
        val sink: FrameOpcodeSink,
        val store: StateStore,
    )

    private class MultiFrameSink : FrameOpcodeSink() {
        val frames = mutableListOf<ProtocolFrame>()

        override fun endFrame() {
            super.endFrame()
            frames.add(frame())
        }
    }

    private fun mount(snapshot: Boolean = false): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        if (snapshot) emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    private fun mountAd(): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(
            MusicPlayerView.make("http://localhost:8080/ad"),
            Environment(PersistentState(store, "session-1")),
        )
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryRendersTracksAndAlbumArt() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Building on Solid Ground"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Rendered Free"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Pathland Dream"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Foundation"))
        assertFalse(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) >= 3)
        assertTrue(anySetPropertyString(frame, Properties.IMAGE_SOURCE, COVER))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryUsesAWindowedList() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.LAZY_VSTACK))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_COUNT, 1000))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_EXTENT, LIBRARY_ROW_HEIGHT))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.FIRST_ITEM_INDEX, 0))
        // Only the initial window (20 + overscan 2) is emitted, not 1000 rows.
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) in 1..40)
    }

    @Test
    fun fitShowsTheSidebarWhenTheParentIsWideEnough() {
        val mounted = mount()
        val slotId = slotIdByMaxThreshold(mounted.sink.frame(), 1024f)
        assertFalse(anySetText(mounted.sink.frame(), "Now Playing"))

        mounted.result.fitInputs()[slotId]!!.accept(2)
        val wide = mounted.sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Up Next"))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
    }

    @Test
    fun playerBarRendersTransportAndSliders() {

/**
 * The player bar's control surface: a centered row of
 * `[rewind] [play-pause] [forward] | [cover art] [track title] | [volume]`
 * over a slim, draggable seek bar that reports progress as a percent.
 */
internal class PlayerControls(
    private val wide: Boolean,
) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val seek = SeekControl(service.position, service.seekRequest)

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 0f) {
            HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 18f) {
                Spacer()
                TransportControls(wide)
                Text("|").fontSize(18f).foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
                TrackInfoView()
                if (wide) {
                    Text("|").fontSize(18f).foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
                    VolumeControls()
                }
                Spacer()
            }
            Slider(
                PercentSeek(seek) { service.currentTrack.get().duration },
                0f..100f,
                seek::onEditingChanged,
            ).frame { width(Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY) }
                .padding(top = 0f, right = 16f, bottom = 0f, left = 16f)
                .accessibilityLabel("Seek")
        }
    }
}

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val current = computed { service.currentTrack.get() }

        return HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 18f) {

                    .fontSize(13f)
                    .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
                    .lineLimit(1)
            }.frame(width = 160f)
        }
    }
}

/**

 *

internal class VolumeControls : Component() {

}

 # pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** November 22, 2026
+**Last updated:** November 26, 2026
 
 Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-core`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
 It owns the app-driven music player and the small sponsored-proxy ad app.
 
 ## Structure
 
 - `music/` — the root `MusicPlayerView` (public, Java-mountable).
 - `music/model/` — `Track`, `Lyrics`.
 - `music/library/` — `LibraryView`, `TrackRowView`.
 - `music/player/` — `PlayerMainArea`, `PlayerBar`, `PlayerControls`,
   `TransportControls`, `TrackInfoView`, `VolumeControls`.
 - `music/player/controls/` — `SeekControl`, `PercentSeek`, `VolumeControl`.
 - `music/service/` — `MediaPlayerService`: per-session player state, playlist,
   `MediaController`, and the environment key shared by the views.
 - `music/lyrics/` — `SubtitlePill`.
-- `music/sidebar/` — `NowPlayingSidebar`, `UpNextRowView`.
+- `music/sidebar/` — `NavigationSidebar` (left), `NowPlayingSidebar` (right),
+  `UpNextRowView`.
 - `ad/` — `AdView`.
 
 ## Shared demo support
 
 - **`DemoTheme`** — the demo's global `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` theme (base + `dark.*`).
 - **`DemoAssets`** — the single embedded copy of the 8 audio tracks, 8 album
   covers, and 8 lyric SRT files under
   `META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/`, plus temp-dir extraction for hosts.
 - **`DemoAssetsTest`** — guards all 32 embedded assets and extraction.
 - **Responsive-size cover assets** — full 440×440 JPEGs remain for the 220×220
   sidebar; separate 176×176 JPEG thumbnails are used by the smaller track-row
   and player-bar images. Both sets are embedded and extracted for web and GTK.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `ViewThatFits`
-  selects narrow (no volume, compact play-only transport), medium (volume), or
-  wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`), with the floating `PlayerBar`.
+  selects narrow (no nav, no volume, compact play-only transport), medium
+  (left `NavigationSidebar` + volume), or wide (left nav + volume +
+  `NowPlayingSidebar`), with the floating `PlayerBar`. The medium threshold is
+  960 pt and wide is 1200 pt so the full player bar fits beside the 220 pt nav
+  (and 280 pt now-playing) sidebar; Now Playing is wide-only.
+- **`NavigationSidebar`** — a static left navigation list (Library, Playlists,
+  Artists, Albums, Songs) authored with the DSL `List` + `SidebarListStyle`.
+  Selection is local visual feedback only (tap/arrow highlight); it does not
+  navigate or filter yet. The selected index/focus live on the shared service
+  so they survive root fit-candidate swaps. The demo theme sets
+  `list.sidebar.background` for light/dark.
 - **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
   `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
   and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
 - **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
   `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
   candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
   and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.

   `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from

 - **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.

 - **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.
 - **Windowed library** — `LibraryView` is a `ScrollView` over a `LazyVStack` +
   paged `ForEach` with a fixed 64 pt row extent; `MediaPlayerService` repeats the
   eight base tracks into a 1000-entry playlist and serves 50-row pages with a
   small simulated latency. Loaded rows render `TrackRowView` (a tappable `HStack`
   highlighted by absolute index); unloaded rows render a skeleton placeholder.
   The live/SSR session uses the `PagedDataSource`; emitter-only unit-test mounts
   keep the in-memory list for determinism. The engine's reactive prefetch keeps
   rows rendered ahead of fast scrolling; the demo has no overscan setting.
   Visible-range reports are coalesced latest-wins and stale pages are cached
   without rendering, so a fast scrollbar drag back and forth reuses the visited
   windows instead of showing blank rows and refetching (ADR-0017).
   **Keyboard library navigation (ADR-0018)** — the library uses the shared
   `LazySelection` component: one roving `FOCUS` tab stop on the service's
   ephemeral `focusedIndex`; ↑/↓/Home/End move it, Enter/tap play, Space toggles
   playback. Selection never requests native focus while the list is unfocused,
   so scrolling/clamping cannot steal focus; tapping a row selects and focuses it
   synchronously before playback. Loaded and skeleton rows share the component's
   wrapper; placeholder rows are keyboard-focusable too. The selected row uses a
   blue background while the list is focused and a neutral gray background while
   it is not; text stays black when unfocused. Every row keeps a stable leading
   speaker icon child and the current track reveals it by opacity, so switching
   tracks cannot accumulate stale icons. List rows use the selected background
   as their keyboard indicator and suppress the generic focus outline. Native player-bar controls
   are explicitly tabbable, so Tab leaves the list and reaches the transport
   controls/seek slider under Safari's default keyboard-nav setting as well as
   Chrome. The volume slider carries an explicit 5% `STEP_VALUE`, so each arrow
   press moves it audibly; the seek slider stays continuous (1% per arrow).

package dev.pathland.demo.music.sidebar

import dev.pathland.core.protocol.Commands
import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
import dev.pathland.demo.music.service.MediaPlayerService

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.LazySelection

import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Spacer
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.VStack
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.background
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.font
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontSize
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.fontWeight
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.foregroundStyle
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.frame
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.listStyle
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.padding
import dev.pathland.view.core.Color as CoreColor
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.List as PathlandList

/** One static navigation section in the left sidebar. */
private data class NavigationItem(val label: String, val icon: IconName)

/**
 * The Apple Music-style left navigation sidebar: a compact, static section list
 * (Library/Playlists/Artists/Albums/Songs) using the DSL `List` with
 * `SidebarListStyle`. Selection is local visual feedback only; navigation and
 * filtering are future work.
 */
internal class NavigationSidebar : Component() {

    private val items = listOf(
        NavigationItem("Library", IconName.FOLDER),
        NavigationItem("Playlists", IconName.LIST),
        NavigationItem("Artists", IconName.USERS),
        NavigationItem("Albums", IconName.GRID),
        NavigationItem("Songs", IconName.MUSIC),
    )

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val selection = LazySelection(service.navIndex, service.navFocused)

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Music")
                .font(Font.largeTitle())
                .fontSize(22f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)

            PathlandList(selection = selection) {
                items.forEach { item -> NavigationRow(item) }
            }.listStyle(SidebarListStyle)
        }
            .padding(16f)
            .background(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.background"))
            .foregroundStyle(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.foreground"))
            .frame(
                width = MusicPlayerView.NAV_SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
                height = Commands.Size.FILL,
            )
    }

    private fun NavigationRow(item: NavigationItem): View =
        HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
            Icon(item.icon)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
            Text(item.label)
                .fontSize(14f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
            Spacer()
        }
}

Now, possible issue: `NavigationSidebar` `VStack` `.foregroundStyle(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.foreground"))` sets COLOR on the VStack; `SidebarListStyle` rows also set foreground token on its own container; redundant but fine. The header "Music" gets sidebar foreground. Good.

Now, possible issue: `Text("Music")` uses Markdown auto-parse; no special chars. Fine.

Now, possible issue: The `List` static with `selection` uses `LazySelection` which sets `focusState` on tap; then `focused(requestFocus)` emits `META::SET_FOCUS` when a nav row is tapped. That will focus the nav row (good) but moving focus away from library row; keyboard nav then applies to nav (arrow keys change section) instead of library. That's expected for a nav sidebar. However, `navFocused` is not reset when the library row is tapped; both could be true, and `focused` signals on both lists could compete. `LazySelection` only requests focus for selected rows; if navFocused is true, the nav selected row continuously requests focus, and tapping a library row sets library focus but nav still requests focus, potentially stealing focus. The nav `focusState` should be cleared when the library is focused, and vice versa. This is an interaction issue. Existing demo has only one selection list; adding a second creates competing focus requests.
- `LazySelection` uses `focusState` gating. If navFocused remains true after tapping a nav item, every re-render will emit `META::SET_FOCUS` to nav row, stealing focus from library. The emitter's `focused` modifier likely emits only on transitions, not every render; but a subsequent library focus could be overridden by nav's true focus binding? Need inspect `FocusRequestView` behavior. It may emit set focus when true on each render or on change. Existing library selection sets `listFocused` true on tap, and focus changes update it via onFocusChanged. If nav list also sets navFocused true and then library tap sets listFocused true, both focus requests could conflict. `onFocusChanged` for nav selected row only applies if selected; when focus moves to library, nav's `onFocusChanged` would set navFocused false (if selected row loses focus). `LazySelection.decorate` adds `.onFocusChanged` only when `isSelected` true (nav selected row), so when it loses focus, it sets navFocused false. Similarly library selected row loses focus, sets listFocused false. So the two lists should coordinate through focus events. Good. The initial nav tap sets navFocused true; then library tap sets listFocused true and nav loses focus -> navFocused false. Fine.
- But `LazySelection.decorate` for nav rows: only selected row gets onFocusChanged; if focus moves from nav selected row to library selected row, nav's selected row loses focus and sets navFocused false. Good.
- Both lists use distinct signals; fine.

- `LazySelection` static List on nav also uses `onKeyDown` for arrows; if nav focused, arrow keys cycle sections. Good.
- The library's `LazySelection` has `onKeyDown` for Space toggles play; nav's onKeyDown default no action. Arrow keys in nav will be consumed by nav (`handleKey` returns true) and not bubble. Good.
- But `LazySelection` `onTap` default null; nav tap sets selected and focus. Good.

Potential issue: Static List with 5 rows uses `LazySelection.decorate` which sets `onTapGesture` on each row. The rows are `<li>` with EVENT_LISTENERS; HTML client will handle tap? It probably handles taps on any element with listeners. Good.

So routing is available. But the music demo doesn't use it; the host route is for metadata only. Adding "real navigation" could be either in-app section switching or route-based. The phrase "real navigation" after adding a sidebar suggests clicking the sidebar should change the content. It could be as simple as a section signal. But "real navigation" might mean URL/deep-link navigation, back/forward, active route highlighting. We need ask.

Also need clarify content for each section. Currently only Library exists. We could:
1. Minimal real navigation: switching sections shows existing `LibraryView` for Library/Songs, and simple placeholder/derived views for Playlists/Artists/Albums. This is "real" section switching but not full content.
2. Build actual section views:
   - Library: all songs (existing).
   - Songs: all songs (could reuse LibraryView but maybe title "Songs").
   - Albums: group tracks by album, show album cards/grid; clicking album? maybe.
   - Artists: group by artist, show artist list.
   - Playlists: static playlists or derived; maybe one "All Tracks" playlist.
   This is more work.
3. URL routing: add Router/NavigationContainer with routes `/library`, `/playlists`, etc.; sidebar rows use `NavigationLink`/router; deep links work; selected row follows route. This is a more complete demo of Pathland's routing. The host demos (Spring/Quarkus) have catch-all routes and SSR; the DOM client mirrors routes. The `MusicPlayerView` could bind router to the host active path signal? The demo root doesn't get the active path; Spring/Quarkus host might provide environment. Let's inspect server APIs for active path/route. Maybe `PathlandSession` has `activePath`? Search.

parts.text:
Interesting: PathlandSession always injects `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`, so a root can bind a router to `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)`. Where is `Platform`? Kotlin/Java. We can use `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)` in a Kotlin component. The demo `MusicPlayerView` can create a router bound to active path. But the root is constructed per session before mount, and active path signal exists in environment at render. We can use `navigator(activePath) { routes... }` inside body? Router should be stable across renders; `navigator` inside body would recreate each render and maybe reset. Better create a `Router` field in `MusicPlayerView` using `Environment.value`? Active path isn't available at construction. Could use a lazy signal binding? `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` environment value is only available during render. We could create router in body once and store field on first render:
```kotlin
private var router: Router? = null
override fun body() {
  val activePath = Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH).get()
  val r = router ?: navigator(activePath) { route("/", LibrarySection) ... }.also { router = it }
  ...
}
```
But `MusicPlayerView` is re-created per session? `PathlandApp.newRoot()` returns new root per session, so field per session. `body()` may re-run; router field stable. The active path signal read in body would subscribe; router bound to active path should re-route. But `navigator(activePath)` builder uses `build(activePath)` and handles external changes. Good.
- But the existing host route is `/` for the music app; deep links `/library`, `/playlists`, etc. would be handled by the server catch-all? Spring demo has a global catch-all? Quarkus IndexResource catch-all? The demo host likely serves any path; but the main app is at `/` and `/app2`; route matching. The `MusicPlayerView` could use routes. The DOM client mirrors `ROUTE` to URL. This would be "real navigation" with deep links.
- However, full routing may be more than needed and could break the demo if host catch-all doesn't serve nested routes. Need inspect Spring/Quarkus catch-all. Search `@GetMapping("/**")` etc.

parts.text:
The server injects `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` and catch-all routes exist. So a real router is feasible. But the user may not want URL routing; they just want sidebar clicks to change sections. We need clarify.

Let's think about what's easiest and most valuable:
- Use `Router` + `NavigationContainer` inside `MusicPlayerView` for section navigation, with routes `/`, `/playlists`, `/artists`, `/albums`, `/songs`. Sidebar rows become navigation actions; selected row follows router. This gives real navigation, deep links, URL updates, and back/forward. But the URL paths would be under the app mount. The Spring demo catch-all handles `/playlists` (and `/app2/playlists`?). The DOM client mirrors route. Good.
- But the main app is mounted at `/` and `/app2`; the catch-all handles both. For Quarkus, deep catch-all handles any path. Good.
- SSR initial route: `MusicPlayerView` reads `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` to seed router; but `Router` should be created with activePath signal. Need inspect how environment values are injected and available during construction vs body. `PathlandSession` wraps root with EnvironmentBinding for ACTIVE_PATH and mounts. The root `MusicPlayerView` is constructed before mount; `body()` called during mount with environment. We can lazily create router in `body()` using `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)`. But the router needs to be created once per component instance and reused across re-renders. `body()` may re-run; a field `router: Router?` could be initialized on first body call. Also, the active path signal is a `Signal<String>` from Environment; `Environment.value` returns a `Signal<T>` (thread-local scoped). We can pass it to `navigator(activePath)`. But if body re-runs, reading `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH).get()` might track route changes and trigger body re-render on every path change, which may be okay. Better use `Environment.value(...)` as signal without `.get()` at router creation? `navigator(activePathSignal)`. Need to get the Signal without subscribing; `Environment.value(key)` returns `Signal<T>` and may be a stable signal from scope. In `body()`, calling `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)` yields Signal; passing to navigator. Does not `.get()` until Router constructor; it does `activePath.get()` to seed and creates an effect. That read occurs during body render; may subscribe body to path changes? It's inside an effect maybe; the Router constructor calls `activePath.get()` directly, outside a tracked context? `body()` is called during `Component.renderNode` inside `Signals.tracked`, so direct `.get()` subscribes. That would make body re-render on navigation, which is fine (and maybe necessary for sidebar selection). But router creation should happen once; if body re-runs, we don't recreate. So field initialization with a function that needs environment is tricky.

Alternative: Put the router in `MediaPlayerService` and initialize it when created? The service is created in `MusicPlayerView` body (`private val service by lazy`), and its `init` uses environment? The service is constructed inside body with `Environment.value` available; could pass activePath into service constructor. But service currently no args and is lazy field initialized on first body call. We could create router in service `init` by reading `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)`? The service is constructed when `service` lazy is accessed in `body`, so environment is active. But `MediaPlayerService` is also used in unit tests with `Environment.DEFAULT` and no ACTIVE_PATH; `Environment.value` returns an `EnvironmentSignal` that returns null-ish? The generic is non-null; might return null cast. Router constructor `Objects.requireNonNull(activePath)` would fail if null. We could use `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` with Environment.value and if captured null, fall back to a local signal. Need robust.
- Or simpler in-app section navigation with `navIndex` as the source of truth; no router/URL. This is less risky and matches current `navIndex` signal. "Real navigation" could just mean section switching.

Need ask the user: do they want URL/deep-link routing or just in-app section switching? Also which sections have real content vs placeholders? This determines scope. Let's ask a couple of questions.

Question 1: Navigation model:
- In-app section switching (recommended? maybe): selected sidebar index drives the main pane; no URL changes.
- Routed navigation (URL/deep-link/back-forward) using Router/NavigationContainer.
- Both (routed is the source of truth for section switching).
Actually routed navigation is "real navigation" and the framework supports it. But it requires route content for each section and maybe tests. The user asked "Can we then add some real navigation to the sidebar?" Likely they want clicks to change content, not necessarily URL. But since Pathland is protocol-first, a demo of routing could be valuable. The router plan docs mention demos. I'd recommend routed navigation as the most "real", but it's more complexity. The user may prefer simple.

Question 2: Content depth:
- Section switching with existing library reused for Library/Songs, plus derived Albums/Artists lists and a simple Playlists placeholder (recommended).
- Full content for all sections (album/artist detail navigation, playlist lists).
- Minimal placeholders for non-Library sections (fast).
Need know what they expect. "Some real navigation" might accept placeholders? Probably not; "real" means actual views. We can implement real content:
  - Library: all tracks (existing).
  - Songs: same list but header "Songs" (all tracks sorted?).
  - Albums: derive unique albums from tracks, show a grid/list of album cards with cover, title, artist; clicking an album could filter songs (second-level navigation) — maybe later.
  - Artists: unique artists, list with icon/cover; clicking could filter.
  - Playlists: static list of a few playlists (e.g., "All Songs", "Pathland Essentials") with maybe derived track counts; clicking could show tracks.
This is a substantial feature.

Maybe scope "real navigation" as section switching only, with actual section views:
- Library = existing library list.
- Songs = same track list (maybe reuse LibraryView with a configurable title) — but duplicate code.
- Albums = group by album, show album rows/cards.
- Artists = group by artist, show artist rows.
- Playlists = a few static playlist rows, maybe each opens a track list? If no second-level navigation, clicking a playlist does nothing, which isn't "real". Could make Playlist section show a list of playlists; selecting a playlist shows tracks? That's nested navigation/state. Maybe too much.

We should ask clarifying questions rather than assume. Let's ask:
1. Navigation model: in-app section switching vs routed URL navigation.
2. Section content depth: all five with derived content vs Library/Songs real + placeholders vs only implement Library and Songs? The user said "some real navigation" — maybe they want the sidebar to actually switch, not necessarily full content.
3. Should section selection persist across sessions (PersistentState) or ephemeral (current navIndex is ephemeral)? If routed via URL, persistence isn't needed. If in-app, maybe ephemeral is fine.

Let's inspect the existing router test/demo to see how a router-bound root is used and if any demo uses `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`. Search tests.

/**
 * The Apple Music-style left navigation sidebar: a compact, static section list
 * (Library/Playlists/Artists/Albums/Songs) using the DSL `List` with
 * `SidebarListStyle`. Selection is local visual feedback only; navigation and
 * filtering are future work.
 */
internal class NavigationSidebar : Component() {

    private val items = listOf(
        NavigationItem("Library", IconName.FOLDER),
        NavigationItem("Playlists", IconName.LIST),
        NavigationItem("Artists", IconName.USERS),
        NavigationItem("Albums", IconName.GRID),
        NavigationItem("Songs", IconName.MUSIC),
    )

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val selection = LazySelection(service.navIndex, service.navFocused)

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Music")
                .font(Font.largeTitle())
                .fontSize(22f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)

            PathlandList(selection = selection) {
                items.forEach { item -> NavigationRow(item) }
            }.listStyle(SidebarListStyle)
        }
            .padding(16f)
            .background(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.background"))
            .foregroundStyle(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.foreground"))
            .accessibilityRole(Roles.NAVIGATION)
            .frame(
                width = MusicPlayerView.NAV_SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
                height = Commands.Size.FILL,
            )
    }

    private fun NavigationRow(item: NavigationItem): View =
        HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
            Icon(item.icon)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
            Text(item.label)
                .fontSize(14f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
            Spacer()
        }
}

              route("/songs") { LibraryView("Songs") }
              route("/albums") { AlbumsView() }
              route("/artists") { ArtistsView() }

## Plan: real sidebar navigation in the music player demo

### Navigation model
Use the existing **Router + NavigationContainer**, bound to the host’s `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal.

Route map:

| Sidebar item | Path | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Library | `/` | existing full track list |
| Playlists | `/playlists` | static playlist list |
| Artists | `/artists` | unique artists from the demo tracks |
| Albums | `/albums` | unique albums from the demo tracks |
| Songs | `/songs` | full track list titled “Songs” |

- Sibling sections use `router.navigate(path)` (no back-stack push).
- Browser back/forward and deep links work through the existing `ROUTE` → `pushState` path.
- Unknown paths fall back to Library.
- **Persistence is the URL**: reloading `/albums` restores Albums; no new `PersistentState` key.

### Wiring
- `MusicPlayerView` creates one router lazily on first render, bound to `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)`, created inside `Signals.untracked` so route reads do not subscribe the whole root.
- Route destinations are fixed view instances (stable identity), created once in the route table:
  - `LibraryView("Library")`
  - `LibraryView("Songs")` (parameterize the existing header)
  - `PlaylistsView()`
  - `ArtistsView()`
  - `AlbumsView()`
- `PlayerMainArea` places `NavigationStack(router)` in the content slot, under the floating player bar, so the bar and now-playing panel persist across section changes.
- `NavigationSidebar(router)` uses a `RouteIndexSignal` adapter (`WritableSignal<Int>`): `get()` maps `router.routeSignal().get().pathOnly()` to the section index; `set()` calls `router.navigate(path)`.
  - `LazySelection` receives this adapter, so tap and arrow-key navigation both update the route.
  - Selected highlight follows the route, including browser back/forward and deep links.
- Remove the ephemeral `navIndex` from `MediaPlayerService`; keep `navFocused` for ephemeral keyboard focus.

### Section content (practical five sections, no drill-down)
- `LibraryView` gains a `title` parameter; `/` and `/songs` reuse it.
- `AlbumsView`: header + unique-album rows (cover, album, artist, song count), `ROLE=LIST`/`LIST_ITEM`.
- `ArtistsView`: header + unique-artist rows (cover, artist, album count), same roles.
- `PlaylistsView`: header + a small static playlist list (“All Songs”, “Pathland Essentials”, “Recently Added”, “Flow”), with cover and song count.
- Add `albums` and `artists` derived lists to `MediaPlayerService` from the base tracks.
- No album/artist/playlist detail routes yet; rows are display-only.

### Files
- Update `MusicPlayerView.kt` (router creation, route table, pass router to nav/main).
- Update `NavigationSidebar.kt` (router param, section paths, `RouteIndexSignal`, remove local-only wording).
- Update `MediaPlayerService.kt` (remove `navIndex`, add `albums`/`artists`).
- Update `PlayerMainArea.kt` (render `NavigationStack(router)`).
- Update `LibraryView.kt` (title parameter).
- Add `AlbumsView.kt`, `ArtistsView.kt`, `PlaylistsView.kt` under `music/library/`.
- Update `pathland-demo-views-kotlin/status.md`.

### Tests
- Add router/deep-link tests:
  - Mount with active path `/albums` → Albums content.
  - Mount with active path `/artists`, `/songs`, `/playlists` → correct content.
  - Unknown path `/nope` → Library fallback.
  - Update the active path signal after mount → content swaps.
  - Click/tap the sidebar “Playlists” row → route changes and content becomes Playlists.
- Keep existing fit/media tests; update only if the extra navigation slot changes expected tree counts.
- Verify medium/wide layouts still show the nav sidebar and Now Playing remains wide-only.

- `mvn -q -P jvm-only test`

## Plan: sidebar label styling + Tailwind-aligned sidebar tokens

### 1. Make `SidebarListStyle` define the row label style

Analogous to SwiftUI `.listStyle(.sidebar)` styling the inner `Label`:

- Add a private `SidebarLabelStyle(selected: Signal<Boolean>) : LabelStyle`.
- `SidebarListStyle.makeRow(...)` applies it to the row content:
  ```kotlin
  content.labelStyle(SidebarLabelStyle(config.selected()))
  ```
- Update the demo sidebar rows to use a real `Label`:
  ```kotlin
  Label(item.label) { Icon(item.icon) }
  ```
- `SidebarLabelStyle` renders:
  - `HStack` with `gap-x-3` spacing
  - `size-6` icon
  - `text-sm` semibold title
  - default/selected icon and text colors
- Any explicit `.labelStyle(...)` closer to the `Label` still wins (environment nearest-wins).
- Document this in `spec/DSL.md` §5.7: a list style may scope a label style over its rows.

### 2. New/updated design tokens

Yes — a small set of `list.sidebar.*` tokens makes sense. They are component-scoped, carry light/dark values, and keep the global semantic palette clean.

| Token | Light | Dark | Tailwind mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list.sidebar.background` | `{color.surface}` | `{color.surface}` | `bg-white` / `dark:bg-gray-900` (already matches) |
| `list.sidebar.foreground` **(update)** | `{base.color.gray.700}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | default `text-gray-700` / `dark:text-gray-400` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.background` **(update)** | `{base.color.gray.50}` | `{base.color.white-a05}` | `bg-gray-50` / `dark:bg-white/5` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.indigo.600}` | `{base.color.white}` | selected text |
| `list.sidebar.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.gray.400}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | default icon |
| `list.sidebar.selected.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.indigo.600}` | `{base.color.white}` | selected icon |
| `list.sidebar.row.radius` **(new)** | `{base.radius.sm}` | `{base.radius.sm}` | `rounded-md` (6px) |
| `list.sidebar.label.gap` **(new)** | `{base.space.3}` | `{base.space.3}` | `gap-x-3` (12px) |
| `list.sidebar.icon.size` **(new)** | `{base.space.6}` | `{base.space.6}` | `size-6` (24px) |

## Standard Token Catalog

The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
"allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).

Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).

### Colors — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), `color.selection` (selected-row
/ selection highlight), and status colors `color.success`, `color.warning`,
`color.danger`, `color.info`.

### Typography — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
| `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |

### Shared control core — Tier 1

Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
apply is ignored.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `control.background` | Control resting background |
| `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
| `control.border` | Control border color |
| `control.border.width` | Control border width |
| `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
| `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
| `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
| `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |

### Per-component tokens

Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
`control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.

**Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
`button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
`button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.

> A composite shorthand such as `button.padding` (two-axis) is renderer-owned:
> the scalar token value types cannot encode a multi-part CSS shorthand. Apps
> that need a scalar override should use the shared control padding tokens or
> per-component properties.

**Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
`input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.

**Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
`toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
`gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.

**Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
`stepper.radius`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
`picker.radius`.

**Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
`menu.radius`.

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

parts.text:
The user asks "Can you suggest meaningful semantic tokens or reuse existing ones? If possible no renderer owned CSS, as this is a composite." They likely want a revised token plan that reuses semantic tokens and avoids renderer CSS. We need suggest either new semantic tokens or reuse existing ones. We should analyze what can be reused:

Existing semantic:
- `color.background` (white / slate-900)
- `color.surface` (white / gray-900)
- `color.text.primary` (gray-900 / gray-50)
- `color.text.secondary` (gray-500 / gray-400)
- `color.border` (gray-200 / gray-700)
- `color.accent` (blue-600 / blue-400)
- `color.selection` (blue-600-a12 / blue-400-a18)
- `color.separator`
- `control.background.hover` is internal; but semantic control hover.
- `control.foreground` gray-900/gray-50
- `control.accent` blue
- `control.padding.*`, `control.radius`, `control.font.*`
- `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`
- `menu.*`
- `color.secondary` indigo-600/indigo-400 (could be used for selected nav accent? Tailwind selected text/icons indigo-600/white. `color.secondary` light indigo-600, dark indigo-400; Tailwind selected dark is white, not indigo-400. Could use `color.text.onPrimary`? Dark white? Hmm.)
- `color.text.onPrimary` = white / slate-900; not exactly white/white. `color.primary` = blue.
- `color.accent` = blue, not indigo. Tailwind uses indigo. `color.secondary` = indigo-600/indigo-400. Selected text in dark is white, not indigo-400. Could use `color.secondary` for selected foreground in light and a new token for dark? Or use `color.secondary` and accept dark indigo-400 instead of white; close? Not exact.
- `color.selection` = blue alpha, not gray-50/white-5.

Maybe we can reuse:
- Background: `color.surface` (white/gray-900) — exact.
- Default foreground: `color.text.secondary` (gray-500/gray-400). Tailwind light default gray-700; gray-500 is lighter. Could use `color.text.primary` (gray-900/gray-50) — too dark/light.  # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 26, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
 signals/computed/effects, router, cross-platform state, and the
 `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. The opcode/wire layer
 (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`) lives in the
 pure-Java `pathland-core` module, which this module depends on. Server and
 renderer modules depend on this module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored
 views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in
 `pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image
 build) carries no JNA.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Opcode/wire layer**: moved to the `pathland-core` module
   (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`). The DSL
   still re-exports the same behaviour through `Text(...)` and the emitter.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly
   typed `Topic<T, S>` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also
   `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)`
   declares an unscoped `Topic<T, GlobalSubject>` with the two-argument
   `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal<T>` backed by a
   session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and
   applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local,
   installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes
   `unsubscribe`, `submit`, `isLive` (SSR vs live), and `onClose` (session
   cleanup). Resolution is lazy when a root view's field initializer runs before
   the context is installed.
 - **Data sources** (`dev.pathland.view.data`): `AsyncDataSource` loads a small
   list from a blocking or `CompletionStage` loader; `PagedDataSource` loads
   offset/limit pages with a bounded cache, in-flight dedupe, `total`/`loading`/
   `error` signals, and window-driven `ensureLoaded`. A page result outside the
   latest requested window is cached (bounded) but not published to the current
   render; stale failures leave the visible loading/error state alone (ADR-0017;
   `PagedDataSourceTest` covers stale success/failure, `PagedFastScrollTest`
   covers fast back-and-forth and a range before the count). Both apply results
   on the session actor, refresh with a stale-result guard, and close with the
   session;
   SSR starts in the loading state and does not run async work. `ForEach(source)`
   renders loaded rows and placeholders; the lazy stack/grid call `prefetch` for
   the initial and adaptive windows. The optional
   `pathland-view-data-coroutines` module adds `fromSuspend` for both sources.
   Cursor/`hasMore` pages and topic invalidation are planned (ADR-0016 Phase 3–4).
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop**: moved to `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore`),
   so server runtimes do not pull JNA.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its
   real parent (not the tree root), so a `VIEW_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a
   pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Eager `ForEach` in stacks**: `VStack`/`HStack` render eager rows as direct
   children, so parent spacing applies between rows. The parent slot tracks the
   collection signal and reconciles row changes; row state remains scoped by item
   key (or index).
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal/state and Kotlin DSL tests
   (which exercise the emitter end-to-end); `pathland-core` owns the
   protocol-manifest, frame-codec, and Markdown tests. `LazySelectionTest`
   covers focus gating, tap/focus ordering, pinning, clamping, 1D/2D navigation,
   concrete grid tracks, adaptive-grid rejection, and the selection/pin conflict
   for all four lazy containers. `ListTest` covers the composite rows, style
   scoping, tokenized chrome (incl. dark-mode tokens), and lazy extent overhead.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`, and the composite `List`.
 - **Styles**: `ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `VideoStyle`, and `ListStyle` are
   environment-scoped (nearest wins). Built-in list styles: `PlainListStyle`,
   `GroupedListStyle`, `InsetGroupedListStyle`, `InsetListStyle`, and
   `SidebarListStyle`; `List` emits `ROLE=LIST`/`LIST_ITEM`, `SELECTED` rows, and
-  adds the active style's row chrome to the lazy item extent. Lazy `List`
-  requires `itemExtent`/`itemExtents`; static `List { … }` is eager.
+  adds the active style's row chrome to the lazy item extent. `SidebarListStyle`
+  also scopes a sidebar label style over its rows (24pt icon, 12pt icon/title
+  gap, 14pt semibold title, default/selected icon and text tokens, rounded
+  selection, 8pt row padding). Lazy `List` requires `itemExtent`/`itemExtents`;
+  static `List { … }` is eager.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `topic(key, subject, initial)`, `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`,
   `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Slider step**: `Slider(value, range, onEditingChanged, step)` emits
   `STEP_VALUE` when `step` is set; the renderers apply it to the native range
   (absent = continuous `step="any"`).
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   **`.focusable`/`.focused`/`.onFocusChanged`/`.onKeyDown`** (focus requests,
   canonical keys), environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation
   intents.
 - **Keyboard focus + lazy pinning (ADR-0018, #204 JVM/web)**: `RenderResult`
   exposes `focusInputs`/`keyInputs`; `InputDispatcher` routes `FOCUS_CHANGED`

   union) and an `onVisibleRange` hook for app-side clamp policy.
 - **`LazySelection`**: all four lazy containers accept an app-owned

   the unfocused visible-range clamp, and `SET_FOCUS` gating. Lazy grids map the
   selected item to its window unit and stop at row/column edges; adaptive grid
   tracks reject selection until a concrete track count is available.
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Verification gaps
 
 - **Media swap coverage (MEDIA-COVERAGE-001):** `MediaProjectionTest` covers
   root projection, surface-first binding, root-rerender identity, and transport
   targeting. It does not establish every structural-swap frame invariant or
   native playback continuity. See the
   [traceability pilot audit](../../../docs/audits/media-controller-identity.md).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **Virtualized lazy stacks (ADR-0014)**: `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing
   a `ForEach` are windowed — extent inference, engine-owned window, keyed
   window reconcile, the window properties, and `VISIBLE_RANGE` routing are
   implemented; lazy grids use a row/column window over the same data source.
   Variable-height stacks are supported with app-declared `itemExtents`
   (`ITEM_EXTENTS`/`FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET`/`TOTAL_EXTENT`); grids use a uniform

   report (ADR-0015); the author does not configure overscan. Focused-row
   pinning is implemented on the JVM/web path (issue #204); Qt and Rust DSL
   parity remain follow-ups.

 - `pathland-core` is the pure-Java opcode/wire leaf: protocol, frame codec,
   events, opcode sink, attributed text, and Markdown.
